rationale: D gives the most economical complete argument, choosing constants before use and concluding through a uniform common-point mass bound integrated over transverse triples. E is similarly precise and efficient, but its stages are less visibly organized. A supplies an excellent overview and clearly separates the slicing kernels, wedge geometry, and exceptional-set estimates; its additional detail remains mostly useful. B is also complete and explanatory, but its preliminary normalization discussion and repeated parameter bookkeeping make it somewhat longer than necessary. C relies on two equation references absent from the supplied context—the direction-pair kernel and point-slice total—whose contents are recoverable from Haar estimates and direct integration, but whose omission weakens completeness and local checkability.
